title: Spherical Lenses and Angular Magnification
notes: **Convex lens:** thicker at the centre, converges parallel rays to the focal point. Positive focal length.
**Concave lens:** thinner at the centre, diverges parallel rays as if from the focal point. Negative focal length.
**Lens formula:** $\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u}$. Note the minus sign compared to the mirror formula, because distances are measured from the lens and sign conventions differ.
**Angular magnification of a magnifier:** $M = 1 + D/f$, where $D = 25\,\text{cm}$ is the near point of a normal eye. A lens with $f = 5\,\text{cm}$ gives $M = 6\times$.

**Why a magnifier works:** the lens allows the object to be placed closer than the near point, so the eye sees a larger angular size. The lens itself does not enlarge the object; it allows the eye to view it from a closer distance.
